key_insight: This paper extends quantum natural language processing to Hindi by introducing a grammar-aware, negation-sensitive compositional pipeline for sentiment classification.
engineering_relevance: It shows how linguistically informed quantum models can be adapted to morphologically rich, low-resource languages beyond English for practical NLP tasks.
method: Manually annotated Hindi sentiment dataset with positive, negative, and neutral labels
Encoded sentences with pregroup grammar and a novel negation-aware compositional grammar in Lambeq
Trained hybrid quantum neural networks for binary and ternary sentiment classification
evidence_signal: The abstract reports effective performance on sentiment classification using a manually annotated Hindi dataset and evaluation in both binary and ternary settings.
watch_item: The approach depends on manual annotation and grammar-sensitive preprocessing, which may limit scalability and robustness across diverse Hindi text domains.
paper_title: Extending the Frontiers of QNLP Beyond English: Grammar-Sensitive Pipeline for Hindi Sentiment Classification Using Compositional Quantum Models
